為什么推薦入住上海迪士尼度假區酒店?
方便刷項目
入住上海迪士尼度假區的酒店都享有三大權益：優先入園(至多提前1小時進入上海迪士尼樂園)、免費酒店-樂園的往返穿梭巴士/船、免費停車。
優先入園1小時可是黃金時間，你能在這1小時把最熱門的項目都提前刷掉。
買1晚含早的朋友，提前刷完熱門項目後，可以回酒店悠閑享用自助早餐，還有機會見到迪士尼朋友們。
買2晚的朋友，下午也可以回酒店休息一下，充好電後繼續入園看煙花、買買買。
樂園酒店的早餐自助餐廳是盧米亞廚房，以《美女與野獸》為主題。
酒店客人的優先入園入口是在單獨的迪士尼小鎮安檢口，人會少很多，不用和早享卡的遊客們卷。
免費行李寄存
在樂園裏寄存行李大概需要80元，而入住迪士尼酒店退房後可以免費寄存行李。
並且可以選擇送到迪士尼樂園入口的遊客中心，一天玩累了之後可以直接帶著行李箱走，不用再回到酒店去取行李了。
方便買買買
兩家酒店一樓都配有商店，還沒入園就可以開始買買買了。另外還可以買到特選商品，特選商品在樂園裏可是需要抽簽中了才能買的。
如果你在樂園裏買了紀念品，又不想拎著購物袋遊玩，那可以使用商品領取服務(免費)，可以送到樂園大門口或者你入住的酒店商店。
各種娛樂活動
2家酒店都配備了遊泳池、兒童遊樂屋、多家餐廳。酒店每天也會有不同的活動可以探索，大人小孩都能玩個大半天。
辦理入住時，小朋友也可以在大堂看迪士尼動畫，遛娃很省心。
沉浸式迪士尼氛圍
樂園酒店更加夢幻，讓你踏進酒店那刻就變身王子公主，改為沉浸在童話世界。最近還新出了求婚套餐，有需求的可以看看。
在樂園酒店，你能隨機碰見米奇和他的朋友們，房間床頭是會“放煙花”的，大堂有迪士尼音樂現場演奏，公區陽台就能看到樂園煙花。
樂園酒店的早餐自助餐廳是盧米亞廚房，以《美女與野獸》為主題。
用餐時還有迪士尼朋友們來每一桌互動。
玩具總動員酒店一定是玩總IP粉的大愛，滿滿的玩總元素。
花園裏有巨大的胡迪、巴斯光年、三眼仔火箭發射台，在色彩明亮的酒店裏走著走著好像自己也變成了安迪的玩具，進入了玩具的世界。
玩具總動員酒店的早餐自助餐廳是陽光食彙，雖然沒有迪士尼朋友來互動，但是餐品也是各種玩總風格。
所以如果想要更省心、更沉浸玩上迪，建議是可以在迪士尼酒店住個1、2晚的，體驗絕對會升級很多。

上海迪士尼為什么值得玩?
1)最新迪士尼，科技感十足
上海迪士尼樂園目前是全世界最新的迪士尼樂園。
雖然上周迪士尼剛官宣了第七座迪士尼樂園(阿布紮比)的消息，但是目前我們上迪還是穩穩最新的、科技感十足的樂園。
特別是加勒比海盜和去年剛開幕的瘋狂動物城園區，各種技術都讓人贊歎，咱們後面慢慢介紹。
2)面積大，項目多
上海迪士尼整個度假區的面積僅次於美國奧蘭多迪士尼。
上迪真的很大，8大園區、2大酒店，還有1個配套的迪士尼小鎮。
我每次去上迪，一整天的步數都在2W打底，所以想要玩遍上海迪士尼，建議是選擇玩兩天。
3)達菲家族元素多
現在提到上迪，第一印象肯定就是我們玲娜貝兒。
達菲家族成員大多數是東迪開始衍生的IP，但是它們在上迪存在感一定是最強的。
專門的七寶商店都有好幾家，更別提買不完的上新商品、季節限定表演、每年都不同的服裝...
雖然作為迪士尼老粉，我更喜歡經典IP。但是達菲家族周邊實在是太可愛了，這幾年也是忍不住買了一櫃子...
所以對於喜歡達菲家族的朋友來說，上海迪士尼絕對能滿足你。
4)超多周邊可以買買買
亞洲的三家迪士尼周邊都很值得買，上新速度快，設計也很在線。
上迪的周邊更是融合了中國特色，你能買到小籠包奇奇蒂蒂或者是上海灘米奇米妮。
達菲家族每年還會有中秋、春節系列。前段時間還出了青花瓷系列呢。
我相信很難有能空手離開上迪的遊客吧。
5)季節限定活動多
每年不同時間都會有限定的季節性活動，四季都會有不同的驚喜。
往年季節活動圖，具體以實際活動為准
給大家Po個全年大概的活動時間，照片都是往年拍的，僅供參考。
春天
春日活動，彩色慶典花車巡遊、賞春賞花。
公主月，可以見到稀有公主王子，還有瘋狂動物城主題活動可以打卡
漫威月，可以見到稀有超級英雄。
夏天
皮克斯月，可以見到稀有皮克斯夥伴。
夏日活動，城堡“潑水節”和達菲朋友夏日巡遊。
秋天
達菲月，達菲和好夥伴們會穿上中秋服飾。
萬聖節，有迪士尼反派夜間巡遊，還可以打扮成迪士尼朋友入園。
冬天
冰雪節，冬日巡遊、米奇大街飄雪、聖誕樹點燈。
元旦，跨年大煙花。
春節，搖擺舞、新年限定大煙花。
夏日活動快來了。大概是6月到8月，覆蓋整個暑假。往年夏日活動比較特色的就是夏日狂歡節城堡秀和繽紛夏日巡遊。
溫馨提醒：准備好雨衣，“澡堂式”水花可不是開玩笑的。
迪士尼朋友們也會換上夏日新裝，期待和你見面。
每年活動也會有一些變動和小驚喜。今年會有什么，可以期待一下哦。
上海迪士尼樂園怎么玩更省心?
作為常年遊客量幾萬的“內卷王”，不管是項目還是互動，排隊時間都很長。
想要玩得省心，接下來劃重點。
1)下載上海迪士尼官方APP
APP最主要的當然是查看地圖和排隊時間，方便計劃下一步去遊玩哪個項目。
APP下載網址：https://www.shanghaidisneyresort.com/information/download-shanghai-disney-mobile-app
除此之外，樂園相關信息基本都能在APP上找到。
比如門票綁定、尊享卡購買、特定商品購買資格抽簽、遊樂項目身高要求、活動演出時間、商店、餐廳、服務設施等等...
2)計劃遊玩路線
計劃好遊玩路線就成功了一半，尤其是對於一天內想刷完大多數項目的遊客來說。
親子遊、情侶遊、朋友遊想打卡的項目會有所不同，所以在這裏也只給大家做一個簡單的路線推薦，具體還得再自己DIY一下。
推薦路線：瘋狂動物城(熱力追蹤)-夢幻世界(小矮人過山車)-寶藏灣(加勒比海盜沉落寶藏之戰)-探險島(翱翔·飛越地平線)-明日世界(創極速光輪)-玩具總動員(抱抱龍沖天賽車)-米奇大街(購物/花車/煙花)
3)購買尊享服務
尊享服務有尊享卡和尊享導覽。
尊享卡相當於走單獨的免排隊通道，最簡單粗暴的氪金力量。每個項目都可以單獨購買尊享卡，或者也可以買尊享套餐。
建議購買尊享卡的項目：熱力追蹤、翱翔·飛越地平線、七個小矮人礦山車、極速創光輪、加勒比沉落寶藏之戰、抱抱龍沖天賽車。
尊享導覽更省心但更貴，對於普通遊客來說也不太建議購買了。
4)入住迪士尼酒店
房間預訂
入住玩具總動員酒店和上海迪士尼樂園酒店，可享提前1小時入園。
這1小時可是黃金時間，可以把最熱門的幾個項目先刷掉，立省幾小時。
提前入園通道是單獨在迪士尼小鎮入口，人會比早享卡入口少很多。
另外也有免費接駁班車/船直接到樂園門口，中途玩累了回酒店休息一下也很方便。
5)購買早享卡
如果覺得尊享卡或者迪士尼酒店超預算了，也可以選擇更實惠的早享卡，大概199元左右，高峰日會更貴一些。
早享卡可以提前1小時入園，和入住迪士尼酒店一樣的權益。
不過早享卡是在樂園正門入園，比起入住迪士尼酒店，需要更早一點去安檢口排隊。
早享卡在入園前7天開放購買，可以去小程序買。一般是0點-0點10分放票。
6)善用單人通道
很多熱門項目是有單人通道的，比如小矮人、熱力追蹤、創極速光輪。一般會比正常排隊時間快一倍以上。
單人通道的定義是補位前面的空缺座位，如果不介意和朋友分開坐的話，是可以一起排單人通道隊伍的。
7)善用無包免安檢通道
上迪的安檢隊伍很長，所以如果不帶包(東西拿手上或者揣褲包裏都可以)的話可以走單獨的無包通道，高峰時間段甚至能省下1個小時。
8)錯峰出行
一般來說，周中的幾個工作日客流量會比較小。
可以通過票價和早享卡價格判斷客流量，價格越高客流量越大。
9)交通選擇
自駕：米奇停車場(14元/小時，112元封頂)，到檢票口需要走大天橋。
迪士尼小鎮停車場(30元/小時，240元封頂)，貴但近，入園離園都很方便。
打車：建議打出租車不要打網約車，到迪士尼出租車上下客點(只有出租車可以到，網約車不行)。離檢票口最近，不需要走大天橋。
地鐵：從市區出發可以乘坐11號線到終點站，步行到檢票口;
從虹橋機場/高鐵站出發可以乘坐市域線到上海國際度假區，再坐巴士/打車。
10）周邊住宿推薦
三簡民宿(迪士尼二期店)
這家具有摩洛哥風格的民宿，乍一看像一座異域城堡。整個民宿都很有設計感。
“三簡”目前共有三期，最好看的就是這二期，房間內部裝修十分上檔次，浴室的設計也特別有品位。最關鍵是民宿還提供免費接駁車接送迪士尼的服務。
地址：川沙鎮牌樓村邱家宅23號
價格：612元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海火星島休閑度假民宿
這是全網被贊爆了的一家民宿，暮色下純白建築仿佛置身於聖托裏尼。民宿從內到外都是純白設計，融合了外星球的元素，特色的樹屋、菠蘿屋，像極了海綿寶寶的家。
公共區域有很多打卡點，天空之境、天梯、無邊泳池和洞穴，非常出片。更重要的是，在民宿露台上就可以看到迪士尼的煙花。
地址：川沙新鎮嶺七路10號
價格：470元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海左汐度假別墅
這家民宿有著童話般的環境，香樟大樹、竹林、草坪，甚至還有一條河作為背景。
室外還有樹屋棧道、拍照水池、透明滑梯、鳥窩、秋千等超多攝影空間，給人一種在置身歐洲度假的感覺。
地址：川沙新鎮果園村434號
價格：632元起/晚
訂房優惠：Trip
上海迪士尼樂園哪些項目值得玩?
上海迪士尼樂園有8大園區：米奇大街、奇想花園、夢幻世界、明日世界、迪士尼·皮克斯玩具總動員、瘋狂動物城、寶藏灣、探險島。
想要一次玩遍所有項目、看完各種演出...是不太可能的，所以給大家推薦一下比較值得玩的項目。直接沖不會錯。
米奇大街
推薦：迪士尼朋友互動、花車巡遊
在米奇大街，最特色的就是你能見到超多迪士尼朋友。喜歡互動的朋友能在這蹲一天。
這裏有各種紀念品商店，在甜心糖果可以買到達菲家族商品。在M大街購物廊能買到經典迪士尼角色商品。
餐飲：米奇好夥伴集市提供麻辣燙、牛排炒面等;琦妙美味屋提供可麗餅、蛋糕等
迪士尼朋友互動：米奇米妮、唐老鴨黛絲、奇奇蒂蒂、高飛布魯托、達菲雪莉玫、星黛露可琦安、傑拉多尼奧樂米拉
奇想花園
推薦：奇夢之光幻影秀
上海迪士尼的煙花秀很震撼大氣，特別是複仇者聯盟那段特別燃。玩上迪一定要看完煙花秀才是最值的。
奇想花園其他的玩樂比較適合小朋友玩，在這也能找到不錯的花車觀賞位置。
其他玩樂項目：小飛象、幻想曲旋轉木馬、米奇俱樂部、漫威英雄總部
餐飲：花間美味、提摩太小吃等小吃
迪士尼朋友互動：米奇、複仇者聯盟英雄
夢幻世界
推薦：七個小矮人礦山車、小飛俠天空奇遇
小矮人過山車建議入園盡早沖，下午排隊時間都會很長。
身高97cm以上的小朋友就可以玩的過山車，基本沒有失重感。途中還能看到小矮人們挖礦工作，小礦車仿佛帶著你穿越進了《白雪公主》的故事。
小飛俠天空奇遇也是很夢幻的寶藏項目，跟著彼得潘一起探險，仙塵灑出來的時候還是很感動的。
旋轉瘋蜜罐現在已經成為“男朋友挨罵打卡點”，來這裏必須要出片!
其他玩樂項目：小熊維尼曆險記、漫遊童話時光、晶彩奇航、愛麗絲夢遊仙境迷宮
餐飲：皮諾丘鄉村廚房提供披薩、豬腳飯等;老藤樹食棧提供烤牛肉、烤雞等
迪士尼朋友互動：迪士尼公主、小熊維尼和他的朋友們
明日世界
推薦：創極速光輪
上海迪士尼樂園可是第一座有創極速光輪的樂園。進入“創”的電子網絡世界，黑暗轉向、室外極速，算是上海迪士尼樂園第二刺激的項目了。如果你看過《創戰紀》電影，會更有代入感。
明日世界主打現代科幻感，在這裏能遇到各位複仇者聯盟英雄們，晚上在E空間俱樂部還有DJ帶你“蹦迪”。
其他玩樂項目：巴斯光年星際營救、太空幸會史迪奇、噴氣背包飛行器
餐飲：星露台餐廳提供漢堡、炸雞等

迪士尼·皮克斯玩具總動員
推薦：抱抱龍沖天賽車、胡迪牛仔嘉年華
抱抱龍沖天賽車我願稱為上海迪士尼樂園最刺激項目，因為失重感很強，特別是第一排和最後一排。喜歡體驗失重感的朋友們一定不要放過這個抱抱龍。
胡迪牛仔嘉年華是最近發現的寶藏項目，以前以為只適合小朋友玩，沒想到“甩驢”竟然這么有意思，配上音樂更歡樂。
“變成玩具”進入玩具們的世界，可以見到最喜歡的玩具總動員朋友們。這裏的色彩飽和度很高，不管是白天、夜晚都很適合拍照。
迪士尼在這裏有自己的“賭場”，比如釣火腿豬、三眼仔打槍、賭抱抱龍。我玩過好多次了，至今沒有中過，有中過的朋友可以分享一下經驗...

瘋狂動物城
推薦：熱力追蹤
全球第一個熱力追蹤，一定要玩。加入動物城警察局，跟著朱迪尼克抓捕壞綿羊。
排隊區很精彩，運用了最新技術的豹警官和牛局長非常逼真。
有時候進入瘋狂動物城園區是需要額外排隊的，如果購買了尊享卡是可以免園區入口排隊 + 免熱力追蹤排隊，所以在客流量大的日子，買熱力追蹤的尊享卡是最值的。
瘋狂動物城是去年新開的園區，各種1:1複刻電影場景，動物城粉狂喜。
還有好多有趣的彩蛋，比如售賣的飲料是百事可鹿、咩年達、7犀，紅綠燈上顯示的不是小人是大象，就連停車位、健身房都設計成大中小來給不同體型的動物用。
雖然這個園區只有一個玩樂項目，但是主題區的有趣程度絕對能硬控你一小時。還有白天限定的動物城生活秀，可以來看看動物們的家長裏短。
餐飲：大象甜品店提供各式甜品;動物城食集可以買到電影裏的爪爪棒冰
迪士尼朋友互動：《瘋狂動物城》朱迪尼克
寶藏灣
推薦：加勒比海盜沉落寶藏之戰
這是我個人認為上海迪士尼最出彩的項目。投影技術+巨幅屏幕，玩的時候真的會不禁發出“wow”。
大船的機制讓這個項目排隊效率很高，基本都在30分鍾以內。結尾還會有2種不同的大結局隨機出現，很有意思。
整個寶藏灣充滿海盜元素，萬聖節期間還有海盜出沒“打劫”，還可以帶上你的迪士尼朋友玩偶一起“蹦迪”。

這是上海迪士尼的老熱門項目了，在熱力追蹤開幕之前，一直是大家早起入園首沖的項目。
跟著雷鳥婆婆進行一場環球之旅，我對非洲大草原的青草味印象特別深刻。

達菲月
在上海迪士尼度假區的10歲生日慶典之際，今年九月的達菲月以達菲和朋友們的溫暖友誼為靈感，邀請遊客加入他們，共赴為期一整個月的全新冒險。
今年達菲月迎來重磅驚喜，上海迪士尼度假區首次攜手享譽業界的上海美術電影制片廠，聯合推出達菲和朋友們的首部動畫微電影。作品將經典國產動畫美學元素與達菲和朋友們的暖心故事巧妙融合，為萌趣夥伴們打造了一段奇妙旅程。此次跨界合作的創意靈感也將全方位落地度假區，融入園區主題裝飾、達菲和朋友們的全新限定造型、獨家商品及特色餐飲體驗中，遊客將處處偶遇驚喜，收獲沉浸式遊玩新體驗。
達菲月期間，度假區將以萌趣滿滿的裝飾迎接遊客。園區內精心打造了多處主題打卡點與拍照牆，融入仙桃、葫蘆、金魚等極具寓意的經典元素，搭配以達菲和朋友們專屬柔和色調精心設計的條幅與絲帶裝飾，氛圍感十足。遊客可置身濃濃秋日氛圍中，邂逅達菲和朋友們，定格溫馨美好瞬間。
達菲和朋友們也將換上融入吉祥紋樣的精美新裝：達菲身著飾有桃子與桃花圖案的服飾;傑拉多尼的服裝繡著荷花與金魚;奧樂米拉的新衣以葫蘆元素點綴;雪莉玫衣服上的飛燕與桃花圖案相映成趣;星黛露的服飾融入了明月與湖波紋樣;可琦安的造型同樣以桃花裝點;玲娜貝兒的衣袂間則點綴著桃子紋樣的刺繡和蝶翼造型的細節。
9月19日至20日及9月26日至29日，度假區更將重磅推出全新的達菲和朋友們主題體驗——“達菲月睡衣派對星光夜”，邀遊客與心愛的達菲萌友們共度特別的夜晚時光。E空間•百事舞台將於晚間呈現“達菲和朋友們的睡衣派對”演出，達菲和朋友們將換上全新睡衣裝扮，在夜空下與遊客分享旅途中的冒險故事，並邀請現場遊客加入一場充滿歡樂的“枕頭大戰”。接棒上演的“達菲和朋友們的特別歡慶”城堡投影秀則以達菲月的經典歌曲《萌聚一起》拉開序幕，達菲和朋友們的身影將點亮奇幻童話城堡，帶領遊客踏上一段穿越四季的旅程。當他們在星空下相聚，璀璨奪目的煙花將於頃刻間綻放，為這場特別歡慶畫上美妙的句點。
驚喜不止於此，度假區還將於今年達菲月期間在奇幻童話城堡舞台呈現全新演出“達菲和朋友們的舟遊記”。延續迪士尼標志性的故事講述與創意，演出將帶領遊客跟隨達菲和朋友們的腳步，踏上一段充滿奇遇和奇妙的冒險之旅。伴隨著全新主題曲的悠揚旋律，遊客將見證七位夥伴各騁所長，齊心協力護送神奇的水晶回家。
自9月5日起的九月每周六、周日，本次全新演出還將限時推出特別專場。上海迪士尼度假區將連續第三年攜手上海滬劇院，為遊客帶來融入經典滬劇元素的專屬版本。這一跨界創新演繹，將迪士尼標志性的娛樂演出與國家級非物質文化遺產——滬劇藝術巧妙交融，生動詮釋底蘊深厚的海派文化精髓。來自上海滬劇院的小演員們將登台獻藝，以地道滬語演繹經典曲目《上海謠》，別具風味地講述獨屬於上海的城市故事，邀請每一位遊客沉浸式邂逅傳統非遺魅力，細細品味曆久彌新的海派風雅與獨特城市韻味。
此外，一系列清甜誘人的桃子主題甜品、搭配精美主題紀念杯的時令特飲、“可琦安的心意餅餅”糕點禮盒，以及更多達菲主題的美食佳肴也將輪番亮相。達菲好友歡慶堂將煥新菜單，帶來“奧樂米拉海島歡歌椰香大蝦飯”和“星黛露絲帶海鮮面”等多款特色菜品。琦妙美味屋也將推出全新風味，邀遊客品嘗百香果鳳梨年輪羊角包、白巧克力奶油蛋糕以及楊枝甘露可夫餅等人氣美食。
逛玩之餘，各式達菲月主題商品也將同步登場。“達菲和朋友們小小奇遇記系列”包含融入中式紋樣的毛絨玩具、掛件、配飾，以及月餅禮盒和家居用品，其中一款與“千年瓷都”景德鎮合作打造、融合了傳統制瓷工藝與迪士尼故事靈感的茶杯格外引人注目。“達菲和朋友們睡衣派對系列”中的軟萌睡衣與睡帽則將助力遊客輕松打造睡衣造型，加入達菲萌友們的夜間派對。
在達菲月期間入住上海迪士尼樂園酒店的遊客還可以沉浸式感受一系列以達菲和朋友們的萌趣世界為主題的奇妙體驗。無論是溫馨治愈的睡前故事、趣味十足的創意手工坊，還是精彩的互動遊戲，抑或是驚喜不斷的酒店探索體驗，每一刻都將化為一場滿載友誼與想象力的奇妙冒險。
玲娜貝兒亮相上海迪士尼度假區五周年
9月23日至29日，度假區將歡迎每一位遊客加入為期一周的歡慶活動，慶祝玲娜貝兒正式亮相上海迪士尼度假區五周年。在此期間，玲娜貝兒不僅將與朋友一同驚喜現身鍾樓，熱情地歡迎遊客們的到來並接收他們的祝福，還將在特別巡遊期間把歡樂帶給巡遊路線兩旁的遊客。
自2021年9月29日在上海迪士尼度假區全球首發亮相以來，這只勇於探索、充滿好奇心、活潑自信的小狐狸贏得了無數遊客的喜愛。五年來，她獨特的魅力和對探索的熱愛不僅激勵了不同年齡段的遊客盡情釋放想象力，勇敢嘗試更多可能性，更將迪士尼的神奇與友誼傳遞至社會各界。

狂歡加碼，十天迪士尼“怪好玩”超級大派對邀遊客創造更多神奇回憶
度假區將於萬聖季期間推出為期整整十天的迪士尼“怪好玩”超級大派對，在10歲生日慶典之際為遊客帶來更多驚奇與歡樂回憶。10月16日至18日、10月23日至25日及10月29日至11月1日期間，遊客可以在樂園內五個熱鬧非凡的“怪好玩蹦迪舞池”盡情歡舞搖擺，在愛麗絲夢遊仙境迷宮邂逅“驚”喜，在節日丘林參加“唐老鴨搗蛋派對”，或者在度假區各處體驗“不給糖就搗蛋”。當夜幕降臨，遊客得以駐足在奇幻童話城堡前欣賞“迪士尼反派魅影秀”，盡享專屬於萬聖季的精彩。
度假區還將推出豐富誘人的限定美味和餐飲體驗，創意黑化美食、節日主題套餐與特色自助輪番登場。除了舌尖上的驚喜，以米奇和朋友們、達菲和朋友們、小熊維尼和朋友們，以及瘋狂動物城為靈感設計的主題商品將同步上新。夜光服飾、南瓜主題單品，舒適秋裝和值得收藏的毛絨玩具一應俱全，每位遊客都能邂逅心儀好物。
樂園之外，萬聖奇趣體驗也將在迪士尼小鎮延續。遊客可以加入“小鎮奇趣大巡遊”的討糖之旅，前往“怪好玩”市集探索好物，或和親友一起拍照留念，定格精彩瞬間。
無論是加入達菲和朋友們的全新冒險，還是暢享為期十天的迪士尼“怪好玩”超級大派對，或是在金秋佳節與親友樂享歡聚時光，這個秋天來上海迪士尼度假區解鎖豐富多彩的季節性活動與體驗，感受度假區10歲生日慶典的更多精彩。
*以上所提及的演出可能會受到實際運營安排、惡劣天氣或其他不可預見因素的影響。例如，在包括但不限於下雨、大風、空氣質量、濃霧、閃電等天氣因素的影響下，可能會推遲或取消整場演出。所有的活動或產品請以活動或產品的詳情頁面為准。
2025上海迪士尼聖誕季
今年的上迪的聖誕季已經開啟了哦，2025年11月21日起至2026年1月3日，如果想要趕個氛圍場(人會比較多)，可以在12月31日-1月1日到樂園，跨年煙花秀等你來解鎖，聖誕季有什么好玩的?
往下看👇🏻👇🏻👇🏻
去迪士尼，大部分人的安排之一應該就是拍拍拍了吧?園區裏的裝飾現在已經全部換上“聖誕款”，白天看著已經足夠好看，到了夜晚燈光一亮，更是直接把氛圍感拉滿了!讓你分分鍾就拍出人生照片!
喜歡合照的寶寶們，米奇和朋友們、達菲和朋友們都已經換上聖誕新造型，等著迎接你～
在聖誕季的每個晚上，米奇、米妮、達菲和玲娜貝兒歡聚奇想花園～你准備好大聲說出“祝你聖誕奇妙”，和他們一起點亮聖誕樹了嗎?
米奇大街今年熱鬧依舊，「聖誕搖擺舞」和「節日快樂, 米奇!」將限時回歸!
Let it go~Let it go~一到冬天，腦海裏就會回響起冰雪奇緣的這個景點歌曲。聖誕季期間，還將有機會在城堡邂逅安娜、艾莎和雪寶，接收她們送來的祝福～
在迪士尼小鎮入口領“聖誕樹尋蹤地圖”，按著地圖指示找到17顆聖誕樹🎄，並蓋章，集齊17個章，就可以得到一個聖誕限定徽章!!這哪個集章人能夠拒絕呀~
除了集章活動之外，迪士尼小鎮還會刷新聖誕老人，想要合照的寶寶們!千萬不要錯過啦!
上海迪士尼樂園吃什么?
樂園餐飲
在樂園用餐比較方便，人均價格在100左右，都會含飲品。
主食個人比較推薦巴波薩燒烤(寶藏灣)的烤豬肋排飯、皮諾丘鄉村廚房(夢幻世界)的豬腳飯、草莓熊餐盒(玩具總動員)的川味炸雞配土豆片。
如果家庭或者朋友結伴出遊，可以選擇點多人套餐，很豐富。
小吃個人比較推薦各種口味的爆米花，是的，迪士尼的爆米花有草莓、小龍蝦、咖喱等等各種口味，聽著奇怪，其實還挺好吃的。
火雞腿基本是入園必吃，其他的玉米熱狗、烤魷魚魚丸、椰奶綿綿冰、泡菜牛肉卷等都可以試試。
迪士尼小鎮餐飲
迪士尼小鎮集合了各種美食，比如全國第一家芝樂坊、唐老鴨歡享小廚、一風堂、桂滿隴、喜茶、阿嬤手作等，選擇會比較多。
在小鎮用餐後還可以從迪士尼小鎮二次入口入園，比到正大門方便很多。
迪士尼小鎮還有最大的迪士尼世界商店，如果在閉園後還沒買盡興，可以再來這消費一波，可以買到樂園裏的絕大部分商品。
其他商店還有樂高、泡泡瑪特等。所以在小鎮也是能逛逛吃吃大半天的。
最後是總結Tips
上海迪士尼樂園客流量大，想要排隊時間短，需要做好路線計劃
上海迪士尼樂園很大，比較費腿，建議可以玩2天
推薦入住迪士尼酒店，有提前入園特權+免費接駁
下載上海迪士尼度假區APP，方便查看排隊時間
選擇尊享服務/早享卡/單人通道/無包安檢，可以減少排隊時間
可以提前准備好一次性雨衣，玩雷鳴山漂流會用上
項目比較推薦熱力追蹤、加勒比海盜沉落寶藏之戰、創極速光輪、七個小矮人過山車
演出比較推薦奇夢之光幻影秀、米奇妙遊童話書
餐飲選擇很多，比較推薦巴波薩燒烤豬肋排飯、爆米花、火雞腿、迪士尼小鎮芝樂坊
購物比較推薦迪士尼世界商店、M大街購物廊、迪士尼酒店商店
入園可以攜帶簡單的食品及飲品，園區內也有提供直飲水
迪士尼小鎮有多家餐飲和購物，可以在小鎮用完餐回到樂園
自駕停米奇停車場，或是迪士尼小鎮停車場(貴但很近)
打車推薦打出租車到出租車上下客點，最近
地鐵市區出發，乘坐11號線;虹橋出發，乘坐市域線
以上就是上海迪士尼度假區的全部攻略了，這是一座科技感和夢幻感交織的樂園。
迪士尼的造夢之路還很長，上海迪士尼樂園二期已經在路上了，每年的季節活動也會有不同的驚喜。所以我們的上海迪士尼攻略也不會到此為止。

title: Shanghai Jing'an Temple Travel Guide: What to See and Do
text:

Shanghai Jing'an Temple Travel Guide: What to See and Do
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Sep. 22, 2026 
Jing'an Temple is one of Shanghai's most recognizable contrasts: a gilded Buddhist temple standing amidst a modern city with heavy traffic and beside one of the city's busiest metro stations.
If you only want Shanghai's classic temple-and-skyscraper photograph, you do not need to buy a ticket for Jing'an Temple. The exterior, nearby plaza, and surrounding streets already give you the city contrast most visitors come for.
Pay to enter only if you want to see the temple as a working Buddhist site: incense, worshippers, timber halls, and Buddhist statues at close range. That is the real choice to make before you arrive.
Is Jing'an Temple Worth Paying to Enter?
Jing'an Temple, Shanghai
Opening hours: 7:30–17:00
Entrance fees: 50 RMB/pp (free admission for seniors aged 70 and over and children under 1.3 meters in height)
Time needed: 1–2 hours
For a first visit, think of Jing'an Temple in two parts:
Exterior visit: free, flexible, and best for the iconic "golden temple in modern Shanghai" image.
Inside visit: paid admission, active worship spaces, and a closer look at the halls, statues, and ritual atmosphere.
Skip It If You Only Want a Quick Photo
The exterior is enough for a strong photograph. You can frame the golden roof with skyscrapers, moving traffic, or people crossing the plaza, creating a picture that says "Shanghai" rather than simply recording a temple facade.
Three nearby viewpoints work particularly well:
1. The pedestrian overpass at Huashan Road and Yan'an West Road gives you the widest city composition. From above, place the temple in the distance and let the traffic and towers fill the foreground. Use the railing only as a compositional line; do not climb it or obstruct pedestrians.
2. The reflecting pool near Exit 14 of Jing'an Temple Station works best when the water is still. Hold your phone low and include both the gold roof and its reflection. This is a simple, social-media-friendly shot that needs no ticket.
3. Jing'an Temple Plaza is better for a closer family or couple photograph. Step slightly away from the entrance flow, keep the guardian lions or roofline in the frame, and avoid blocking people who are arriving to worship.
Night view of Jing'an Temple, Shanghai
For daylight, the temple roof usually reads most clearly when the sky is bright.
For a darker, more cinematic image, arrive around sunset. However, to photograph the temple illuminated at night, you will need to visit between 6:00 PM and 10:00 PM on a Friday or Saturday.
If photography is your priority, a China Highlights guide can place these viewpoints into your walking route instead of sending you inside simply because the temple appears on a standard sightseeing list.
5-Day Shanghai, Hangzhou and Suzhou Explore the Elegant China
Enter If You Want to See an Active Buddhist Temple
A close-up look at the architectural details of Shanghai's Jing'an Temple.
Inside, Jing'an Temple makes sense when you want to understand it as an active Buddhist temple rather than a photogenic building.
You may see people lighting incense, praying, and moving quietly through the halls. Keep your voice low, follow signs and staff instructions, and never photograph worshippers, monks, or sacred objects without permission.
Touring the temple usually takes about one hour for the main spaces. With children, or if you want time to observe the architecture, allow longer. If your Shanghai schedule is already packed, the exterior is the better choice.
Mahavira Hall
The Mahavira Hall is the main focus of most visits. It houses a colossal silver statue of Sakyamuni Buddha—standing approximately 8.8 meters tall and weighing around 15 tons—which serves as the temple's most prized treasure.
Worshippers come here to pay their respects and pray for their families' safety and well-being, seeking to avert misfortune and clear away life's troubles and obstacles.
Jade Buddha Hall and Guanyin Hall
The side halls offer a more intimate contrast to the main hall's scale, named for a large white-jade Buddha and a Guanyin statue carved from camphor wood.
These details are best appreciated slowly. Look at the material texture, the expressions on the statues, and the relationship between the statues and the surrounding woodwork.
Worshippers typically visit the Guanyin Hall to pray for harmony in their personal relationships, while seeking physical health and the purification of karmic obstacles at the Jade Buddha Hall.
Jing'an Vajrasana Pagoda
Located in the northwest corner of the temple complex, this seven-story square pagoda is another important part of the temple's skyline.
Beyond admiring its architectural beauty, you may also join the faithful in circumambulating the pagoda three times in a clockwise direction to pray for smooth endeavors and family harmony.
Etiquette for Visitors
Please dress modestly when entering the temple;
Step over the threshold rather than stepping on it;
Light incense with your left hand; do not blow out the flame with your mouth—extinguish it by gently waving the stick instead;
Please speak in a low voice while inside the halls;
Do not block the pathways leading to the altars or incense burners;
Do not photograph Buddha statues, monks, or worshippers without permission.
9-Day Beijing ,Xian and Shanghai Tour China Family Classic Tour 
How Long Do You Need at Jing'an Temple?
30–45 minutes: exterior views and photography;
About 1 hour: a basic inside visit covering the main halls and atmosphere;

One or two days let you see Shanghai. Three days let you experience it.
We would like to describe Shanghai in three layers:
The historic Bund and old city streets.
The leafy, everyday life of the Former French Concession.
The futuristic energy of Pudong.
Each layer deserves its own day, so you can slow down, wander, and actually feel the contrast between them. 
Follow our three-day plan that takes you through all three layers—one day for the past, one for the present, and one for the future—at a pace that leaves room for discovery, not just checklist-ticking.

Start your morning on the Bund, walking along the historic waterfront with a guide who will bring the old buildings to life—from the grand Astor House Hotel to the iconic Peace Hotel and the former HSBC Building.
To help you create lasting memories, we offer postcards and stamps for you to choose from, so you can send a piece of the Bund home to someone special.
After lunch near Nanjing Road, continue your day to Yu Garden, a classical Chinese garden hidden in the old city. Wander through its winding corridors, koi ponds, and bizarre rockeries, while learning about the garden's remarkable story of destruction and rebirth.

Start your walk at Fuxing Park, where a century ago French residents sipped coffee behind iron gates while Chinese locals could only look in from outside. Today, the park is for everyone.
Walk along Sinan Road, lined with vintage villas and quiet doorways, where your guide will share the stories of the families who once lived here. You can pause for a while at a corner café tucked inside a lilong alleyway, where modern coffee shops and bakeries now breathe new life into the old lanes.

Two Days in Shanghai: Focus On the Core Sights

Having two days in Shanghai means you have time to feel the city from two distinct layers, but you still can't afford to squeeze all the highlights or even a side trip from Shanghai city center without sacrificing experiences or the relaxed pace.
The Bund and the Former French Concession, representing the past and lively present, are both excellent candidates for this kind of immersive experience.
On Day One, you can walk the Bund, step inside the grand buildings of the "International Architecture Exhibition," and uncover the stories behind them. After lunch, continue to the old city and Yu Garden—all within walking distance—and return to the Bund before 6 PM for a stunning sunset view of the skyline, if the weather is clear.
On Day Two, immerse yourself in the leafy streets of the Former French Concession. Walk along Sinan Road, pass by the legendary mansions that once belonged to Shanghai's most powerful figures, and stop at Tianzifang's maze-like alleyways, where traditional lilong housing now hosts boutiques, galleries, and cafés.
If you are more interested in the futuristic side of Shanghai, feel free to replace one day that may seem less appealing to you, to enjoy the panoramic views of the urban area from Shanghai Tower's peak and high-tech gadgets at Pudong.
Should You Spend More Than 3 Days in Shanghai?
For most travelers, three days is enough to cover Shanghai's highlights without feeling rushed. But if you have four or five days, you have the luxury of going deeper.
Extra days allow you to hop on Shanghai's galleries, take a day trip to a nearby water town like Zhujiajiao or Tongli, or simply spend an unhurried afternoon in a neighborhood park watching locals go about their daily routines.

Shanghai Weather in September 2026: Mild, Quieter, and Tips
 Written by
 Carper
 Updated Apr. 29, 2026 
Shanghai's September marks the beginning of autumn and sees the retreat of summer crowds.
September's average temperature ranges from 21°C (70 °F) to 27°C (81 °F), with an average of 8 rainy days having 3.9 inches (99 mm) of precipitation. 
Summer heat still lingers in early September, and it is normal to see temperatures reach over 35°C (95 °F). Data from September 2025 shows a peak of 38°C (100°F) on September 6th.
But you can expect a gradual drop from mid-September, by the end of September, to around 21°C (70 °F).
September is also the tail month of Shanghai's typhoon season. Though the peak time falls at late-July and late-August, you still need to try your luck and there is a possibility of encountering a typhoon.
Is September a Good Time to Visit Shanghai?
Our clients in Yu Garden in September, Shanghai
September is one of the best months to visit Shanghai. 
Rainfall decreases, crowds are much thinner than in July and August, queues at attractions are shorter or even nonexistent, and the weather begins to cool to a more comfortable level. 
But not all of September is the same. Choosing the right window within the month can make a real difference. Let me walk you through it.
1. Early September (1–10): Summer Heat Lingers, But Crowds Have Already Left
Early September still feels like summer. Daytime highs often reach 28–30°C (82–86°F), and in 2025, it was still usual to exceed 35°C (95°F), though humidity is noticeably lower than in August. 
The good news? Summer vacation is over. 
Most Chinese students are back in school, so tourist numbers drop sharply. You'll find shorter queues at popular spots like the Oriental Pearl Tower and Yu Garden. 
If you don't mind the lingering warmth, this is a great time for a quieter trip. Just plan outdoor activities for the morning or late afternoon, bring a handheld fan, and stay hydrated.
2. Mid-September (11–20): The Best Window with Mild Days and the Fewest Crowds
The French Concession, Shanghai
If your schedule is flexible, aim for mid-September. This is the window I recommend to our clients, friends, and family. 
Daytime temperatures average 24–27°C (75–81°F), with low humidity and gentle breezes. Evenings are cool enough for a long walk along the Bund or a night cruise on the Huangpu River.
Crowds are at their lowest of the month, and hotel rates are still reasonable. Whether you want to explore the French Concession, visit Zhujiajiao Water Town, or simply wander the city streets, this is the time to do it.
2-Week Shanghai, Suzhou, Hangzhou, Guilin, Xian, and Beijing Tour Touch Chinese Elegance 
3. Late September (21–30): Festivals Bring Back the Crowds
The Mid-Autumn Festival in 2026 falls on September 25–27. Many Chinese travelers take extra days off to extend the holiday with the following National Day holiday (October 1–7). 
Popular attractions get crowded again, and hotel prices begin to rise. If you're traveling in late September, book your flights, hotels, and attraction tickets at least 2–3 months in advance. 
Also, expect larger crowds, especially at family-friendly places like Shanghai Disneyland and Zhujiajiao. The weather remains pleasant, so with good planning, you can still have a wonderful time. >>Contact us to start planning your trip
4. Will I Be Affected by the Typhoon?
September is still within Shanghai's typhoon season (July to September). However, typhoons are much less frequent than in August. 
When they do occur, they usually happen in early September and pass within 1–3 days. By mid-September till the end, the risk is very low. 
So if you're traveling in early September, pay more attention to check the weather forecast a few days before departure and keep your itinerary flexible. A small buffer can save you from unexpected delays.

What to See and Do in Shanghai in September
Citywalk in Shanghai: A Time-Travel Contrast
The night view of the Bund, Shanghai
September's mild weather is perfect for walking. I suggest two very different but equally fascinating routes.
The Bund: Witnessing the Fusion of History and Modernity
Start at the Bund. Walking along the Huangpu River and taking in the historic colonial buildings on the Puxi side, you will see that the architecture is from the 1920s and 1930s. 
Then turn around and look across the river. There stands Pudong's futuristic skyline: the Oriental Pearl Tower, Shanghai Tower, and Jin Mao Tower. It's a stunning contrast between old and new Shanghai, all in one view.
The French Concession: The Legendary Life of China's Godfather
Head to the French Concession, where we will take you through Du Yuesheng's life, who became a Chinese mob boss from a nameless.
Many will describe the French Concession as quiet and romantic. It is full of charm to wander through tree-lined streets and see trees forming a green shade overhead, adorning villas and secluded courtyards.
Stop at Basement FG Vintage, the predecessor of Sanxin Company that was founded by Huang Jinrong, Du Yuesheng, and Jin Tingsun. 
You may be hard to trigger by wandering through an ancient building, not until our guide tells you the story behind it, including its inextricable link to the opium trade in the French Concession of Shanghai.
Enjoy Shanghai's Parks and Wildlife: Strengthen Family Bonds
Shanghai Wild Animal Park
As crowds recede, September's comfortable days make it a great time to visit urban green spaces and wildlife attractions, especially suitable for multigenerational trips.
Shanghai Disneyland
You can expect shorter queues with pleasant weather during this period, and the park starts decorating for early autumn. 
If you want to fully experience the whole park within one day without two-hour waits, such as the Zootopia: Hot Pursuit or Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, this is your window.
Shanghai Wild Animal Park
Located in Pudong, this is one of China's best safari parks. You can take a feeding truck through the free-roaming animal zones and see lions, tigers, and bears up close. 
If Chengdu isn't on your itinerary, come here to see giant pandas. 11:30 AM and 2:30 PM are the pandas' "snack time," which is also the best time to observe them. At these times, the pandas will surround their keepers, begging for food, appearing exceptionally lively and adorable.
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Welcome to the only aquarium in the world with a dedicated China exhibit featuring Yangtze River basin species. Here, you'll see rare Chinese sturgeon, Yangtze alligators, and other native aquatic life. 
It's also one of the largest man-made seawater aquariums in the world, large enough for a family afternoon of exploration or a rainy backup plan during early September.
Experience Mid-Autumn Festival Traditions
Take a cooking class to learn how to make mooncakes
If you're in Shanghai during the Mid-Autumn Festival (September 25–27, 2026), we would like you to participate in the traditional activities rather than just watching.
We'd like to teach you how to make traditional Shanghai mooncakes (or soup dumplings (xiaolongbao) if you don't like mooncakes), and enjoy hairy crabs with chrysanthemum tea. 
After a satisfying meal, let's go to Yu Garden to enjoy the Mid-Autumn Festival lantern display, and admire the bright moon hanging in the sky together.
What to Pack and Wear in Shanghai in September
September in Shanghai brings gradually cooling weather, from warm early in the month to pleasantly mild by late September. 
Packing light layers should be the smartest choice. Bring a few short-sleeved T-shirts for warmer daytime, and comfortable sneakers for walking. And you'll need a light jacket or a long-sleeved shirt for cooler mornings and evenings, especially if you're planning to enjoy a Huangpu River night cruise.
Rainfall is low in September, but a small folding umbrella is always a good backup. The sun can still be strong, especially in early September, so don't skip sunscreen, a sun hat, and sunglasses.

Shanghai Attractions
Shanghai, as the most modern international metropolis in China, boasts a wide variety of attractions that are scattered throughout the city. Foremost among them are the views along the Huangpu River, which divides Shanghai into two distinct worlds. The east bank presents a futuristic atmosphere because of numerous uniquely designed skyscrapers reshaping the urban skyline, with the highest one standing at an impressive 632 meters (2,073 feet). While on the west bank exudes a retro and historical charm, for there are rows of century-old European-style architectures along the Bund, retelling the stories of old Shanghai.
Moreover, Shanghai is home to the iconic traditional Chinese garden, Yu Garden; China’s most prosperous commercial street, Nanjing Road; and the most advanced Disneyland over the world, Shanghai Disneyland Park. If you fancy historical treasures, then don't miss the Shanghai Museum East. Wandering around the Zhujiajiao Ancient Town, you can experience the authentic local life and witness Shanghai’s tenderness. In short, there are always different appearances of the city waiting for your exploration.
Top Attractions
The Bund – Time-honored European Architectural Complex On the Bund along the west bank of Huangpu River, there stand a series of distinct and magnificent classical European-style architectural complexes, attracting millions of tourists every year. Over a century ago, they mushroomed as foreign-funded business and government offices, transforming this area into a bustling "Far East Wall Street". Now, most of them have become fashionable landmarks for high-end brand stores, luxury hotels, art galleries, restaurants, and leisure venues, standing opposite the modern skyscrapers across the river. When the lights ablaze at night, the entire Bund is dressed in a golden brilliant coat and the skyscrapers on the opposite riverbank also shine colorfully; the beautiful scenes on both sides are reflected on the Huangpu River, forming a stunning dazzling picture. At this time, taking a sightseeing boat and enjoying the charm of this night view while feeling the gentle breeze is the most pleasant experience.
Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street - the No. 1 Commercial Street in ChinaThe Nanjing Road Pedestrian Street, known as "the No.1 Commercial Street in China", is one of the most bustling commercial streets in Shanghai. With the total length of approximately 1.5 kilometers (1,600 yards), it is a paradise for tourists to shop and enjoy delicious food. Strolling through it, you can witness how the contents of this commercial thoroughfare has seamlessly transitioned from international luxury brands to contemporary Chinese fashion, from daily necessities to high-end electronic products, and from century-old Shanghai delicacies to Michelin-starred cuisine. While you are drawn to the various shops, the pleasant tinkling sound will direct your attention to the distinctive sightseeing vehicle – the retro-style trolley. Riding on it, you can leisurely travel through this bustling street that combines both European classical elements and modern artistic atmosphere.
Yu Garden – Classical Chinese Garden in Shanghai DowntownYu Garden stands out among the modern buildings and bustling cityscape in Shanghai downtown. It was built over 450 years ago during the Ming Dynasty (1368 - 1644) and is one of the most renowned classical gardens in China. The garden features exquisite pavilions, rockeries, ponds, curved bridges, corridors, embossments, and carvings, showcasing the essence of traditional Chinese garden art. Among them the most interesting treasure is the Exquisite Jade Rock – it has a history of more than one thousand years, with a peculiar shape and dense small holes all over it, creating a mysterious atmosphere. Besides, the garden also preserves a large number of antique furniture and famous calligraphy and paintings as cultural relics from the Ming and Qing (1644 - 1911) dynasties.
Shanghai Museum East – Comprehensive Presentation of Chinese CivilizationShanghai Museum East has a comprehensive collection of Chinese ancient relics that not only cover all Chinese historical periods, but also feature extensive varieties ranging from bronzes, ceramics, jade, sculptures to calligraphy & paintings. The Great Bronze Cauldron, as one of the must-see artifacts, has mysterious animal patterns outside and eulogistic inscriptions inside, showcasing the superb craftsmanship of bronze forging existed over 3,000 years ago. Looking at the Sky Blue-glazed Plate manufactured more than a thousand years ago, you will be amazed how ancient Chinese managed to create such a smooth porcelain in vivid color without machines. Additionally, there is another branch, Shanghai Museum on People's Square, which now has transformed into a hub of world relics where you can admire exquisite antique Chinese furniture, diverse handicrafts from different Chinese ethnic minorities, as well as overseas cultural heritage such as the Olmec Colossal Stone Head and Greenstone Figures from Ancient civilizations of the Americas.
Zhujiajiao Water Town – Shanghai's VeniceZhujiajiao Ancient Town, about 1.5 hours’ drive away from Shanghai downtown, was built along the waterways and so is known as "Shanghai's Venice". The town has a history of over 1,700 years and preserves a great many architectural complexes from the Ming and Qing dynasties. Everywhere in the town are small bridges and flowing water, with white walls and black tiles decorating both sides. The whole water town presents a quaint and peaceful landscape of the typical Southern China style, contrasting sharply with the urban hustle and bustle of Shanghai. Tourists here can’t help but slow down and fully appreciate the beautiful scenery. At sunset, taking a traditional rowing boat to cruise and watching the red lanterns on both banks light up one after another would be an extremely enjoyable experience.
Shanghai Disneyland Park – Fairyland in RealityShanghai Disneyland Park, as the first Disneyland in Chinese mainland and the sixth in the world, is the newest and most modern one. Apart from the classic globally shared amusement areas and entertainment facilities such as Pirates of the Caribbean and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train, it has also created a globally exclusive "Zootopia" themed area. The entire park uses high-precision projections and VR interactive technologies to bring the magical world from fairy tales to reality, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in the game scenarios following the main characters in the animated films. Moreover, Shanghai Disneyland Park is filled with Chinese elements, such as the Tai Chi-wielding Donald Duck, Disney characters transformed into the twelve Chinese zodiac signs, and the integration of classic operas of Peking Opera in the musicals, providing you with a unique playing experience different from other Disneyland parks.
Shanghai Tower – the Tallest Skyscraper in ChinaShanghai Tower is situated on the east bank of the Huangpu River in Lujiazui. Standing at a height of 632 meters (2,073 feet), it ranks the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world. The entire building features a spiral ascending streamline shape. Looking afar, it seems like a giant dragon in silver scales leaping out of the river and hovering beneath the sky. It's fascinating that many people give it the nickname "egg whisk" due to its unique design. Shanghai Tower has a total of 127 floors on the ground. Every year, countless tourists come for a visit, taking the world’s fastest elevator to reach the "Top of Shanghai Observator" on the 118th floor in just about 55 seconds, and then enjoying a 360-degree panoramic view of Shanghai.

The Bund Shanghai
 The Bund, the landmark of Shanghai, is a 1.5-kilometer (0.9-mile) long, narrow strip of waterfront along the Huangpu River in the city center, primarily composed of the riverside promenade and historic buildings of diverse architectural styles dating back a century. Featuring both retro and modern elements, and with its brilliantly illuminated and bustling night view being truly breathtaking, the Bund is regarded as the symbol of Shanghai and becomes one of Shanghai’s must-visit attractions.
The Bund Facts 
Our Tour Group at the Bund
  3-Day Private Shanghai Tour from $509
  1 Day Shanghai Highlights Tour from $109
More Shanghai Tours  Location: on the west bank of Huangpu River, stretches from the Waibaidu Bridge over the Suzhou River in the north to Yan’an East Road in the south. 
 Highlights: best night view in Shanghai; European style building clusters; perfect sightseeing spot along the waterfront
 Opening hours: it’s an all-year-round attraction and opens all day.
 Light opening hours: 19:00-23:00 from May to October, and 18:00-22:00 from November to April. During holidays such as New Year and National Holiday, or special events, the lights usually will be turned on earlier and turned off later.
 Time needed for sightseeing: 1-2 hours
History of the BundBefore Shanghai was opened as a trading port in 1843, the Bund was just a muddy and rudimentary riverbank. Later, in the mid-late 19th century, with the establishment of the British and French concessions, the infrastructure of the Bund gradually improved. Today, many Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical style architectural complexes in this area originated from the masterpieces of British architects and foreign investors. These buildings used to be residences of international renowned financial institutions such as banks, trading companies and insurance companies during the concession period, which stimulated the economic development of the Bund and even Shanghai. Therefore, this region is also known as the “Wall Street of the East”. In 1943, the Bund ended its centurial concession period and gradually welcomed new large-scale improvements and developments. It has not only retained its historical and cultural heritage but also incorporated modern elements, becoming an image of Shanghai and China’s economy, and also a popular tourist destination for visitors.
Best Time to Visit the BundThe best time to visit the Bund is in the early morning and at night. Strolling along the Bund in the early morning allows you to avoid the crowds and experience the genuine daily lifestyle of the local people; while visiting at night you will see a totally different version of the Bund that is bustling and embellished with golden neon lights. Lucky enough, you might even be able to witness a large-scale drone show. Night Views of the Bund 
Best Things to Do in the Bund
Joining Locals Doing Morning ExerciseElderly locals doing morning exercise have become a regular sight on the Bund. Here you can see them strolling, jogging, practicing Tai Chi or flying kites. Particularly, near the Huangpu Park, many energetic locals would wave the colorful dragon-shaped ribbons. Getting up early to join them is a delightful way to experience the authentic local way of life.
Strolling along the Waterfront Avenue and Admiring the Historical ArchitecturesThe Bund is renowned for its unique collection of international architecture. From the eclectic Asia Building (now China Pacific Insurance Co., Ltd.) in the south to the Former British Consulate General Building in the north, each building narrates a timeless story in its own distinctive style. As you stroll along the Bund, you’ll first be captivated by the grand exteriors of these row upon row of structures. And if you learn their stories, it feels like watching a long yet unforgettable classical film.

Appreciating High Rises across the Huangpu RiverLooking across the Huangpu River, what catches your eye are high-rise buildings that are completely different from the Bund architectural complex and full of modern science and technology, including the Oriental Pearl Tower, the World Financial Center, Jinmao Tower and Shanghai Tower. These four buildings are the tallest skyscrapers in this city, dominating the skyline and forming an excellent backdrop for taking pictures on the Bund. Pudong Seen from the Bund Western-style Achitecture along the Bund  
Admiring the Sunset on Waibaidu BridgeWaibaidu Bridge, the first steel-framed bridge in China with a history of over a century, showcases the beauty of the industrial era. At sunset, the bridge’s unique triangular geometric structure, combined with the afterglow of the setting sun and the shimmering Suzhou Creek below, creates an excellent vantage point for you to take photos.
Dining at a Rooftop Restaurant of the BundThere are many open-air restaurants along the Bund, which are perfect places to enjoy delicious food while taking in the beautiful views of the Bund. For instance, the terraces of the Bund No.3, No.5 and No.6 offer various styles of dining options for you. Here, you can enjoy a romantic dining atmosphere and take some wonderful photos of the Bund and the modern skyline of Pudong Area.
Experiencing the Bund Sightseeing TunnelThe Bund Sightseeing Tunnel crosses the Huangpu River, connecting the Bund and the Lujiazui commercial district in Pudong New Area. This is the first cross-river sightseeing tunnel in China, integrating transportation and tourism functions. Inside the tunnel, different themed experience scenarios are set up through advanced technologies. Tourists can take the transparent sightseeing cable car and experience the futuristic tunnel while speeding across both banks of the Huangpu River at high speed. Shanghai Tower
 The Shanghai Tower, as China’s tallest and the world’s third tallest skyscraper, is located at Lujiazui, Pudong New Area, Shanghai. It serves as a monumental landmark in Shanghai, integrating commercial, office, hotel, exhibition, entertainment, and sightseeing functions. From the observation deck atop the tower, you can take in a panoramic view of the entire city—admiring the winding course of the Huangpu River, the retro architectural clusters of the Bund, and the towering high-rises in Lujiazui. With a total height of 632 meters, the tower consists of 127 above-ground floors and five underground levels. Its footprint covers 30,368 square meters, equivalent to the size of 4.5 standard football fields. The Night View around Shanghai Tower  
Exterior & Design Features Shanghai Tower The architectural structure of the Shanghai Tower is spiral-shaped, resembling a coiling dragon when viewed from a distance. This unique design, which breaks away from the monotonous form of traditional skyscrapers, not only stands out in architectural aesthetics but also boasts exceptional practicality. The gradually rotating structure significantly reduces wind resistance, ensuring the tower remains upright and stable even in strong winds. Additionally, the foundation consists of 955 piles, each reaching 86 meters in length, driven into the soft soil to securely support the tower’s weight of 800,000 tons—equivalent to the combined weight of 70 Eiffel Towers.
The building’s facade features a double-glazed curtain wall system to enhance its thermal insulation, heat resistance, and soundproofing performance. During the day, it reflects dazzling brilliance under sunlight, while at night, its lighting system activates, casting an array of colorful lights that create a stunning sightline for the entire Shanghai skyline. From a distance, you can be awestruck by its towering, luminous, and transparent structure; while inside the building, you can gaze at the magnificent cityscape through the fully transparent glass curtain wall.
Best Things to Do within Shanghai Tower
Experience the “Top of Shanghai” Sightseeing TourThe “Top of Shanghai” sightseeing tour starts from the Shanghai Tower Exhibition Hall on B1. The highlight of this hall lies in its status as a display space integrating culture, technology and architectural art. Through various high-tech display methods, visitors can gain an in-depth understanding of Shanghai’s urban development trajectory and the construction mysteries of the Shanghai Tower. On the B2, there are three ultra-high-speed elevators—OB1, OB2, and OB3—capable of reaching speeds of up to 20.5 meters per second. Taking these elevators allows visitors to reach the 118th floor, the Top of Shanghai Observatory Deck, in just 55 seconds. From the observation deck, you can overlook through the transparent glass curtain wall and take in the magnificent views of the entire Shanghai urban area. At sunset, you can experience the romance of the sunset’s afterglow.   Top of Shanghai Observatory Deck Ultra-high-speed Elevator of Shanghai Tower  
Appreciate the Light and Shadow Show of the Damper in the Tian Shi 632 Art SpaceThe Tian Shi 632 Art Space, renowned as the “world’s highest art space” located on 125-126 floors of Shanghai Tower, integrates music, light, projection, lasers, and other multi-dimensional artistic expressions to create an interactive experience for your senses. Between the two floors, there is the world’s only open damper exhibition area, equipped with technology driven interactive installations and artistic light shows, allowing visitors to fully appreciate the charm of this 1,000-Ton Tuned Mass Damper, known as the “Eye of Shanghai”. Shanghai Tower and Other Skyscrapers in Pudong
  More Pictures of Skyscrapers in Pudong New Area   
Enjoy a Leisurely “Book Café” Time in Duoyun Books on the 52th FloorDuoyun Books features unique visual design and tranquil reading space. Most importantly, the bookstore itself is free of charge. In addition, there are two observation decks in the north and south, which can be accessed unlimited times with a dining consumption receipt of the store. If you want to have a rest after sightseeing in crowded areas of this building, here is a perfect option. You can order a cup of coffee and dessert which costs about RMB 30-50, and enjoy reading or just sit near the observation deck with beautiful views, spending some leisure time.
Note: Duoyun Books requires advance reservation on the WeChat official account. The opening hours are 10:30-20:00 every Monday, and 10:00-20:00 from Tuesday to Sunday.  Duoyun Books Observation Deck of Duoyun Books  
Admire Ancient Chinese Artifacts in Shanghai Guanfu Museum on the 37th FloorShanghai Guanfu Museum has four permanent exhibition halls: the Porcelain Hall, the East-West Hall, the Goldware Hall, and the Sculpture Hall, as well as a temporary exhibition hall. The Porcelain Hall mainly features porcelain from different dynasties in northern and southern China, allowing you to appreciate the beauty of ancient Chinese porcelain craftsmanship. The East-West Hall displays over 100 exhibits, primarily export porcelain and furniture, showcasing the cultural exchange and fusion of craftsmanship between China and the West from the 16th to the 18th centuries. The Goldware Hall features over 200 exhibits, mainly ancient Chinese gold artifacts, supplemented by gold artifacts from China’s neighboring countries. The Sculpture Hall primarily displays 47 Buddhist statues from ancient China and neighboring countries.  If you are visiting the Shanghai Tower and happen to be interested in ancient Chinese artifacts, don’t miss this museum! 
  Shanghai Tower in Pudong  
Enjoy Fine Meal at Michelin Three-star Maison Lameloise on the 68th FloorYou are recommended to go to Maison Lameloise on the 68th floor, the first overseas branch of France’s famous century Michelin three-star restaurant, to experience the luxury food combining French cooking methods and fresh local ingredients from Shanghai. The business hours of this restaurant are from 11:30 to 13:30 from Friday to Sunday and from 18:00-20:30 daily. The best time to enjoy delicious food here is at dusk. You can book a seat by the window, which is perfect for taking photos with the backdrop of breathtaking scenery of sunset and city lights.
Functional Zones of Shanghai Tower No. Functions Zone 9 (Levels 118-126) Viewing and equipment areas Zone 7-8 (Levels 84-115) Hotel floors and apartments, offering upscale accommodations and related services Zones 2-6 (Levels 8-81)  Office areas Zone 1 (Levels 1-5)  Comprehensive commercial and service area Basements (B1-5) B1-2 are mainly used as a brand commercial area, business and life service area, as well as a transportation hub connecting Metro Line 2, Line 14, and surrounding buildings such as Jinmao Tower to the north and Shanghai World Financial Center to the east;
 B3-5 are mainly used as parking lots and equipment areas.  
How to Get to Shanghai Tower?
By Metro1. Take the Shanghai Metro Line 14 to Lujiazui Station, exit from Gate 9A, and walk approximately 10 minutes to reach the destination.
2. Take the Shanghai Metro Line 2 to Lujiazui Station, exit from Gate 6, and walk for about 10 minutes to reach the destination.
By Bus1. Take the City Sightseeing Bus Line 2, get off at Jinmao Tower Station, and walk south for about two minutes to reach the destination.
2. Take No.791, 870, 961, 961 Shuttle Bus, or 985, get off at Dongtai Road Station on Lujiazui Ring Road, and walk west for about 1 minute to arrive.
By FerryYou can take the Dongjin Line (Jinling East Road Ferry Dock— Dongchang Road Ferry Dock) or the Dongfu Line (Fuxing East Road Ferry Dock — Dongchang Road Ferry Dock), then disembark at Dongchang Road Ferry, cross the road to the opposite side, and walk north along Shibu Street for about 6-10 minutes to reach the destination. Ferry on the Huangpu River  
Shanghai Tower Tickets & Opening Hours / Shanghai Tower Opening Hours 08:30-22:00 Daily; Ticket Sale Stops at 21:30 Tickets for the Top of Shanghai Observatory Adult: CNY 180 Chilren between 1 - 1.4 meters (3.3 - 4.6 feet): CNY 90 FREE for children under 1 meter Note: The damper exhibition area requires separate ticket, CNY 88 per person. 
You can use your passport ID to book tickets on the WeChat official account, but the process may be cumbersome and only WeChat payment is supported. If you don’t understand Chinese and want worry free ticket purchasing, you can consult travel agencies such as TCG.
 Shanghai Tower Ticket Booking
 Ticket Office of Shanghai Tower  
Tips for Visiting Shanghai Tower1. As a landmark building in an international metropolis, Shanghai Tower tends to be crowded especially during holidays and weekends, there may be awkward situations such as overcrowding, long queues, or sold-out tickets. Therefore, in order to enter smoothly, it is strongly recommended to purchase tickets and make reservations at least one week in advance.
2. Make sure that minors follow adults closely to avoid getting lost in the crowd.
3. The entrance and security checks are at B2, so avoid carrying flammable and explosive items such as alcohol and lighters. For your convenience, the luggage storage is available at the ticket office and the underground shopping corridor on B2. Luggage Storage of Shanghai Tower 
4. Considering the fast speed of the elevator to the Top of Shanghai Observatory, it is easy to experience uncomfortable reactions such as tinnitus and ear swelling while riding it. In general, this situation is normal and will disappear after exiting the elevator; but tourists with heart disease or fear of heights are not recommended to go there.

Shanghai Ferry
The Huangpu River running through Shanghai, divides the city into two parts - Pudong New District (east of the river) and Puxi Area (west of the river). The three islands of Chongming, Changxing, and Hengsha under the jurisdiction of Shanghai are separated from the main by the Yangtze River. As a result, ferries play a very important role in the city's transportation.  
Huangpu River Ferry 
As many bridges, tunnels, and subways are built, people have much more choices when traveling across the Huangpu River. However, ferryboats with 100-year's history are still popular choices for pedestrians and cyclists because of their convenience and low price. At present, there are in total 17 ferry lines serving nearly 40 ferry stations along both sides of the Huangpu River, providing links between Pudong and Puxi.

Best Time to Visit Shanghai
Best Months to Visit Shanghai: March-May; October-NovemberMarch to May and October to November are the best times to visit Shanghai, since they boast cozy and favorable weather, vibrant and colorful scenery, and not very crowded attractions overall. View of the Bund  
March to MayShanghai gets rid of the damp and chilly winter and ushers in spring during this time. Temperatures rise to around 10-25°C (50-75°F), making for a warm and comfortable climate. You can enjoy outdoor sightseeing without bundling up in heavy layers or worrying about intense heat. Moreover, rain won’t pose much of a threat to your trip, as this season typically features light showers and enjoys plenty of sunshine. Furthermore, the city transforms into a veritable world of flowers, with cherry blossoms, tulips, magnolias, rapeseed flowers, and many other blooms filling the streets. 
During these months, as long as you avoid the Qingming Holiday in early April and May Day holiday in early May, you can experience Shanghai at its most romantic with a relatively quiet atmosphere. Zhujiajiao Water Town in Spring  
October to NovemberAt this time of year, Shanghai has completely shed the stifling heat of summer, with temperatures hovering between 15 and 22 degrees Celsius (59-72 degrees Fahrenheit) - an extremely comfortable range. Besides, both the rainy season and typhoon season have ended, and this period has minimal rainfall, dry air, and excellent visibility, making it ideal for all kinds of outdoor activities. Moreover, Shanghai offers a unique natural spectacle during this season: autumn foliage. With these golden leaves, attractions like the Yu Garden and Zhujiajiao Water Town become even more appealing.
Apart from the National Day holiday in early October, visitor numbers in Shanghai remain not very high during the rest of this period. Yu Garden in Early October  
Best Months to Enjoy a Quiet and Cheap Trip: December-February, Except the New Year and Chinese New Year Period 
These three winter months mark the slack tourism season of Shanghai. The biggest advantage of the off-season is, of course, that it offers a quieter and more relaxed experience thanks to fewer tourists. Specifically, visiting either the Bund or the Yu Garden during this time, you can enjoy your trip at a leisurely pace and don’t need to make any effort to dodge crowds while taking photos. Additionally, if you choose to visit Shanghai during these months, your overall travel costs will be significantly lower: hotel rates will be discounted, airfares will be cheaper, and attractions like the Yu Garden will offer off-season pricing.
The New Year period in late December, as well as the Chinese New Year Festival period in January or February, are not part of the off-season; on the contrary, these times are very crowded. If you are looking for a quiet trip, be sure to avoid these two periods. 
Note: This period is considered the slack season because the weather in Shanghai is quite cold. Therefore, be sure to pack plenty of warm clothing for your trip and do not stay outdoors too late in chilly evenings. Quiet Disneyland Park in Winter Yuyuan Bazaar with Fewer Tourists  
Not-Recommended Months to Visit Shanghai: Mid-June to Mid-September
First, this is the hot summer, with high temperature above 30°C (86°F) nearly every day, and usually around 35°C (95°F). Combined with high humidity, the weather feels uncomfortably hot. It’s no exaggeration to say that within half an hour of staying outside, you will feel sticky all over.
Second, Shanghai experiences frequent rain during this period. Mid-June through early July marks the city’s plum rainy season, when persistent drizzles and sudden downpours fall from time to time. Your itinerary will be significantly disturbed: outdoor sightseeing will be inconvenient, visibility will be low and the sky will almost always be overcast, and some shows and parades at Disneyland Park may be canceled. From late July to mid-September, Shanghai is likely to be affected by typhoons, which force you to stay indoors.
Furthermore, it’s important to note that Shanghai is packed with tourists in July and August, as this period coincides with China’s summer vacation. Inevitably, travel expenses will also be significantly higher than usual. Crowded Nanjing Road Even in Morning  
OK Months to Visit Shanghai: Early June & Late September
Though early June also belongs to summer, the climate of Shanghai is not very hot. Besides, the city has not entered the rainy season yet. In late September, the weather gradually cools down, and the typhoon season ends. So, these two periods both feature not bad weather conditions. 
The Most Crowded Periods You Should AvoidThe busiest travel periods you are highly recommended to avoid are the three long holidays - the Chinese New Year holiday in January or February, the May Day holiday from May 1 to 5, and the Chinese National Day holiday from October 1 to 7. How crowded will Shanghai be at these times? At popular attractions like the Bund, Nanjing Road, and the Yu Garden, you’ll practically be pushed along by the crowd; meanwhile, you’ll have to wait in line for two to three hours for the most popular items at Disneyland Park. In addition, hotel rates typically rise to two or three times their usual price.
New Year’s Day, Qingming Festival in early April, Dragon Boat Festival around mid-June, and Mid-Autumn Day in mid to late September are also full of visitors, though not as many as the above three holidays.

粉白夢境，最是極致浪漫的詮釋
櫻花以300多天的沉寂，換來7日的絢爛綻放。初綻時，如少女指尖的胭脂，羞澀而熱烈;盛放時，千朵萬朵同時綻放，將天空染成溫柔的粉色暴動;飄零時，則如粉色的雪，認真而決絕。當其他花朵還在追求持久，櫻花已領悟“向死而生”的美學。
觀賞地點：薔薇園櫻花林、盆景園、蘭室、南區溫室周圍、北區等。
觀賞品種：東京櫻花、美國櫻、大葉早櫻、大島櫻等約80個品種。
玉蘭
蟄伏大師，時間之外的孤勇者
玉蘭的花苞從冬至春蟄伏百日，綻放時花瓣舒展至極。氣溫連續3天超過15℃，花苞便突然炸裂，沉默的等待化作驚雷。玉蘭品種繁多，當早春的玉蘭類華麗謝幕，星花玉蘭、二喬玉蘭等也陸續登場，延續春日玉蘭的盛宴。
觀賞地點：木蘭園、蘭室、盆景園、牡丹園。
觀賞品種：二喬玉蘭、星花玉蘭、紫玉蘭等近100個品種。
海棠
跨界啟示，從分類學到萬有引力
海棠自古受文人墨客青睞，其詩詞既抒情又蘊含植物學智慧。古典海棠四品：西府海棠、垂絲海棠、木瓜海棠、貼梗海棠。其中前兩者為蘋果屬，後兩者為木瓜屬，一定程度上可以理解為海棠其實是不同種類蘋果和木瓜的統稱，這是否讓你想到牛頓的蘋果與萬有引力?又是否憶起《詩經•衛風•木瓜》……
觀賞地點：薔薇園、北區、熱帶植物館(番木瓜)、藤蔓園(野木瓜)等。
觀賞品種：垂絲海棠、西府海棠、木瓜海棠、貼梗海棠、湖北海棠等。
牡丹
人間富貴花，極致之美顯霸道
牡丹被譽為“花中之王”，兼具盛唐華貴與植物學精密演化。即使單朵花養分消耗巨大，卻仍選擇盡情綻放，以吸引高階傳粉者。芍藥與牡丹相似，常使人混淆，二者實為“木本與草本的姐妹花”。而荷包牡丹花似荷包，葉似牡丹，卻與牡丹親緣甚遠。
觀賞地點：牡丹園、草藥園。
觀賞品種：中原牡丹、江南牡丹、伊藤牡丹、芍藥、荷包牡丹等。
桃花
夭夭其華，灼灼其姿，偏沾了人間煙火
東風過處，桃花醒來，似將三月春光揉碎綴滿枝頭。遠望如緋雲墜地，近觀如美人初妝。粉、紅、白，各色爭豔。最妙是那將開未開的花苞，緋色羞怯，如少女抿唇藏笑。全開後，花蕊淌蜜，引蜜蜂蝴蝶跌跌撞撞赴宴。
觀賞地點：薔薇園、單子葉植物區、植物大樓周圍、岩生植物園等。
觀賞品種：碧桃、蟠桃、‘菊花’桃、‘品虹’桃、‘灑金龍柱’桃等。
杜鵑花
花中西施，姹紫嫣紅
四月，杜鵑以驚世之美，為春添上濃墨重彩。那漫山遍野，非含苞之羞，而是盛放之極致——深紅如朝霞，粉紫似煙雨，純白若新雪。杜鵑，花中西施，野性難馴，肆意張揚。杜鵑鳥以歌喚山川，杜鵑花以血染春，共譜四月天最動人之曲，演繹生命之絢爛與守望。
觀賞地點：杜鵑園、廣玉蘭大道、北區、亞高山植物館。
觀賞品種：杜鵑花、錦繡杜鵑、雲錦杜鵑、馬銀花、馬纓杜鵑等約100種。
瓊花
維揚獨株，四海無雙
煙雨江南，瓊花悄綻，玉潔冰清，傳為隋煬帝所求之絕世容顏。北宋王禹偁筆下的古瓊花，乃神話孤品，僅生於揚州，後神秘消亡。明清後所稱“瓊花”，實為“聚八仙”，即今之瓊花(Viburnum keteleeri)。瓊花八朵不孕花環中央可孕花，智慧生存之道也。
觀賞地點：桂花園、蕨類園、廣玉蘭大道、北區、盆景園。
觀賞品種：瓊花、繡球莢蒾、台東莢蒾、煙管莢蒾等。
木香與酴醾
香雪海，春日暴雪
木香與酴醾，唐宋詩詞中之“雙生花”，世人青睞，風雅之爭亦相親。萬千細碎白黃，染世界為甜夢。單朵雖小，千萬同心，如香雪傾瀉，金簾垂掛。無玫瑰之刺，卻以柔韌藤蔓征服廊架。花瀑之下，悟最美征服非鋒芒，最動人之力乃柔軟。藤花滿架，乃春之無字情詩。
觀賞地點：藤蔓園、薔薇園、草藥園、盆景園。
觀賞品種：木香花、酴醾、金櫻子、黃木香花、紅木香、重瓣空心藨等。
紫藤
疑是紫色星河垂人間
當春風掠過廊架，紫藤蘇醒了，看似枯幹的藤幹，萬千花穗垂落，似銀河傾瀉，如雲霞停駐，每一串花序都是春天揮毫寫下的狂草，在光影中搖曳，將時光染成深淺不一的紫，詮釋“柔韌的力量”。
觀賞地點：環保區遊船碼頭、桂花園、藤蔓園、薔薇園、盆景園等。
觀賞品種：紫藤、銀藤、多花紫藤品種。
來上海植物園，沉浸式賞花悟道。不妨做個自然筆記，記錄每一個美好瞬間。向花兒學習時間管理和生存智慧，做一個隨時准備綻放的人。

走进豫园，这座古典的中国园林隐藏在上海老城的中心地带。

常見問題解答 
 我在上海转机游览需要多少小时？ 
为了获得顺畅的旅程，我们建议至少预留 8-10 小时的转机时间。
如果您计划参观更多景点或选择游览上海中心大厦等自选项目，建议预留较长的转机时间（10-12小时）。我们会根据您的时间安排调整行程。 
 没有中国签证可以参加这个旅行团吗？ 
在很多情况下，答案是肯定的。上海为符合条件的过境旅客提供免签政策，允许他们经中国前往第三国。
我们建议您提前查询您的国籍和中转停留时间。如有需要，我们很乐意在您预订前提供建议。 
 如果我的航班延误了怎么办？ 
别担心。这是上海私人转机游览，我们会监控您的抵达时间。

title: Lujiazui - Shanghai Financial Center Skyline Icon - LoongWander
text:
Located on the banks of the Huangpu River in Pudong New Area, Shanghai, Lujiazui is the financial center and iconic cultural tourism hub of the city. Geographically, Lujiazui spans from Pudong South Road and the Ring Road in the east, Dongchang Road in the south, to the Huangpu River in the west and north, covering a total area of approximately 1.7 square kilometers. As a core landmark of Shanghai's Pudong development and opening-up, Lujiazui is characterized by its dense cluster of super high-rise buildings, a comprehensive financial service system, and unique riverside landscapes. It houses several skyscrapers among the world's tallest, with the Shanghai Tower reaching a total height of 632 meters, making it the tallest building in China and the third tallest in the world; the Shanghai World Financial Center stands at 492 meters, and the Jin Mao Tower at 420.5 meters. These three structures collectively form the "Lujiazui Three-piece Set" urban skyline. As of 2025, the Lujiazui area is home to over a thousand financial institutions and dozens of regional headquarters of multinational corporations. It also integrates diverse tourism functions such as riverside leisure, urban sightseeing, and cultural experiences, welcoming more than ten million visitors annually, solidifying its status as the core destination of Shanghai's urban tourism.
History and Culture
The name Lujiazui derives from Lu Shen, a scholar of the Hanlin Academy during the Ming Dynasty, whose family once resided here. Additionally, the area lies at a bend in the Huangpu River, resembling a "mouth," hence the name. In modern times, Lujiazui was once a major center for light industry and a hub for wharf storage in Shanghai, witnessing the initial development of modern Shanghai's industry and preserving a small number of relics of modern industrial architecture, serving as important evidence of Pudong's historical context.
In 1990, the national strategy for the development and opening-up of Pudong in Shanghai was officially launched, designating Lujiazui as a national-level financial and trade zone. Since then, it has embarked on a transformation journey from a traditional industrial zone to an international financial center. Over the past three decades, Lujiazui has evolved from an area of farmland and old factories into a modern urban district integrating finance, trade, tourism, and culture. Its development journey is a vivid epitome of China's reform and opening-up, and it has fostered the unique cultural core of Lujiazui—the "Pudong Spirit" of daring to explore, innovate, and take the lead.
Today, while retaining its core financial functions, Lujiazui continuously integrates Shanghai-style culture and modern urban culture. Urban public spaces such as the Bund Riverside Avenue, various art galleries, and cultural exhibitions and performances have transformed Lujiazui into not only a financial hub but also a vital platform for cultural exchange in Shanghai, achieving mutual empowerment between economy and culture.
Main Attractions
Shanghai Tower
Standing at 501 Yincheng Middle Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Tower has a total floor area of 578,000 square meters and a height of 632 meters. Designed by the American architectural firm Gensler, it was officially put into use in 2016. With 118 floors above ground and 5 underground floors, the tower integrates office, hotel, sightseeing, and commercial functions. Its iconic "Shanghai Skyline" observation deck is located on floors 118-119, at an altitude of 546 meters. Equipped with the world's fastest super high-speed elevator (reaching a speed of 18 meters per second), it takes only 55 seconds to travel from the underground 1st floor to the observation deck. Visitors can enjoy a 360-degree panoramic view of Shanghai, making it the premier high-altitude sightseeing spot in Lujiazui.
Shanghai Tower
Shanghai World Financial Center
Located at 100 Century Avenue, Lujiazui, the Shanghai World Financial Center stands at a height of 492 meters with 101 floors above ground and 3 underground floors, covering a total floor area of 381,600 square meters. It officially opened in 2008. Its most distinctive feature is the "wind tunnel" shape at the top. The observation facilities are located on floors 94 (423 meters), 97 (439 meters), and 100 (474 meters), among which the 100th-floor suspended observation corridor uses transparent glass floors, allowing visitors to directly view the urban landscape beneath their feet. It is a highly distinctive high-altitude sightseeing experience spot in Lujiazui. The tower also accommodates international financial offices and commercial facilities.
Shanghai World Financial Center
Jin Mao Tower
Located at 88 Century Avenue, Lujiazui, the Jin Mao Tower has a total height of 420.5 meters with 88 floors above ground and 3 underground floors, covering a total floor area of 290,000 square meters. Completed and opened in 1999, it is an early super high-rise landmark building in Lujiazui. The tower integrates traditional Chinese pagoda architectural style with modern skyscraper design. The 88th-floor observation deck, at a height of 340.1 meters, features an open-air high-altitude viewing platform, offering a close-up view of the Huangpu River and the cityscape on both banks. The tower also houses the Grand Hyatt Shanghai, occupying floors 53 to 87, making it one of the tallest hotels in the world and setting a benchmark for the integration of business and sightseeing.
Jin Mao Tower
Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui
Stretching approximately 2.5 kilometers from Dongchang Road Ferry to Pudong South Road, covering an area of about 100,000 square meters, the Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui, is an urban riverside public space integrating leisure, sightseeing, and ecology. Adjacent to the Huangpu River and facing the Bund International Architecture Exposition across the river, the avenue is equipped with hydrophilic platforms, viewing walkways, green landscapes, and various leisure facilities. Visitors can stroll along the river to admire the Huangpu River scenery and the Lujiazui skyline, making it a popular spot for photographing Shanghai's urban landscape. It is open 24 hours a day and serves as the core area for leisure activities for both residents and tourists in Lujiazui.
Bund Riverside Avenue, Lujiazui
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Located at 1388 Huansha Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium covers a total floor area of approximately 20,500 square meters. It is a national AAAA-level tourist attraction that officially opened to the public in 2002. The aquarium features a 155-meter-long underwater tunnel, one of the longest in the world, showcasing over 500 species and 10,000 aquatic organisms from all five continents and four oceans, including rare species such as the Chinese sturgeon and Chinese alligator. It serves as an integrated marine-themed exhibition hall combining display, popular science, and education, welcoming over 2 million visitors annually.
Shanghai Ocean Aquarium
Shanghai Disney Store
Located at 180 Fenghe Road, Lujiazui, the Shanghai Disney Store (Lujiazui Branch) is the first flagship store of Disney in Mainland China, covering a floor area of approximately 5,000 square meters. The store features a comprehensive range of Disney-themed products, from classic cartoon character merchandise to limited-edition souvenirs, making it a popular destination for family outings and Disney fans. Its architectural exterior incorporates classic Disney elements, serving as a distinctive node of Lujiazui's commercial and cultural tourism.
Shanghai Disney Store
Recommended Itinerary
Recommended one-day classic itinerary for Lujiazui: Arrive at Lujiazui Metro Station (Line 2) at 9:00 AM. First, visit the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium (approximately 2 hours) to get up close with marine life. At 11:30 AM, head to the Bund Riverside Avenue and walk along the Huangpu River to the Dongchang Road Ferry section, enjoying the Bund and Lujiazui skyline. Take a break in the riverside leisure area for a light meal. At 1:30 PM, visit the 88th-floor observation deck of the Jin Mao Tower (approximately 1 hour) to experience high-altitude sightseeing. At 3:00 PM, go to the Shanghai World Financial Center to check out the 100th-floor suspended observation corridor (approximately 1.5 hours). At 4:30 PM, visit the Shanghai Tower to reach the "Shanghai Skyline" observation deck (approximately 1 hour) and enjoy the panoramic view of Shanghai during sunset. After 6:00 PM, head to Lujiazui Center L+Mall or the New World Department Store for dinner. Afterward, enjoy the Bund night view from the Bund Riverside Avenue to conclude the day's journey. If time permits, you can add the Disney Store and Lujiazui Center Green Space to create a two-day itinerary. On the first day, focus on high-altitude sightseeing and riverside landscapes; on the second day, focus on the aquarium and commercial experiences.
Travel Tips
Best travel time: Spring and autumn (March-May, September-November), when the weather is pleasant and visibility is high, ideal for high-altitude sightseeing. For night views, it is recommended to visit on Fridays and Saturdays, when the Bund and Lujiazui light shows are more spectacular, running from 6:00 PM to 10:30 PM.
High-altitude sightseeing tips: Choose 1-2 out of the Shanghai Tower, World Financial Center, and Jin Mao Tower to avoid redundant experiences. It is advisable to book tickets 1-2 days in advance through official platforms to save time waiting in line.
Family-friendly travel tips: Prioritize the combination of the Shanghai Ocean Aquarium and Disney Store. The aquarium is recommended to be visited for 2-3 hours, avoiding weekends and holiday peaks, as the venue is less crowded at 9:00 AM when it opens daily.
Photography tips: The best spot to capture the Lujiazui skyline is near the Dongchang Road Ferry section of the Bund Riverside Avenue. The optimal time to photograph the Bund and Lujiazui together is one hour before sunset ("golden hour"). For high-altitude panoramas, it is recommended to bring a wide-angle lens. The 118th-floor observation deck of the Shanghai Tower allows the use of non-professional photography equipment.
Dining tips: Dining options in Lujiazui are relatively expensive. You can choose to eat at comprehensive malls such as the New World Department Store and Lujiazui Center L+Mall, or opt for light meals and coffee shops in the riverside area.
Travel duration: A full-day visit (8 hours) is recommended to cover all core attractions. For in-depth experiences (such as hotel afternoon tea or detailed exploration of exhibition halls), a 1.5-2 day itinerary is suggested.
Notes
High-altitude sightseeing notes: The observation decks of the Shanghai Tower, World Financial Center, and Jin Mao Tower prohibit the carrying of flammable and explosive items and large luggage (luggage exceeding 20 inches). Glass walkway areas are off-limits to visitors wearing high heels. Children must be accompanied by adults, and children under 1.2 meters are eligible for free admission at some venues.
Crowd control: During holidays (such as the Spring Festival and National Day), crowd control measures will be implemented in the core area of Lujiazui, with some roads possibly temporarily closed. It is recommended to check announcements from the Pudong New Area Cultural and Tourism Bureau in advance and travel during off-peak hours.
Transportation tips: The Lujiazui Metro Station (Line 2) will implement passenger restrictions during holiday peak hours. It is recommended to exit at Pudong South Road Station (Line 14) or Shangcheng Road Station (Line 9) and walk to the destination to avoid congestion.
Weather tips: High-altitude sightseeing is highly affected by weather. If encountering haze or heavy rain, visibility will be significantly reduced. It is recommended to check the Air Quality Index (AQI) before traveling; the viewing effect is optimal when the AQI is below 100.
Property safety: In crowded areas with many tourists in Lujiazui, please keep valuables such as mobile phones and wallets safe. In open areas such as the Bund Riverside Avenue, be cautious of falling objects from drones, kites, and other high-altitude items.
Facility usage: Public facilities such as benches and restrooms on the Bund Riverside Avenue are free to use. It is prohibited to occupy public spaces for vending or camping; please abide by public place management regulations.
Transportation
Metro: Take Shanghai Metro Line 2 to Lujiazui Station (Exit 1, 2, or 6 leads directly to the core area). Take Line 14 to Pudong South Road Station (Exit 4, walk approximately 800 meters to the Bund Riverside Avenue). Take Line 9 to Shangcheng Road Station (Exit 1, walk approximately 1 kilometer to the Lujiazui Central Area).
Bus: Bus routes in the Lujiazui area include Routes 81, 82, 583, 799, 939, 961, etc. Key bus stops are Lujiazui Ring Road Fenghe Road Station and Lujiazui Metro Station, which provide direct access to various attractions.
Ferry: Take the East Jin Line ferry from the Jinling East Road Ferry in Puxi's Bund to the Dongchang Road Ferry, which takes approximately 10 minutes. After landing, walk for 5 minutes to reach the Bund Riverside Avenue, offering a unique way to experience Huangpu River transportation.
Self-driving: Parking lots in the core area of Lujiazui mainly include the New World Department Store Parking Lot, Shanghai Tower Parking Lot, and Jin Mao Tower Parking Lot. Parking spaces are in high demand during holidays; it is recommended to prioritize public transportation.
Taxis/Ride-hailing: Ride-hailing drop-off points in Lujiazui are mainly concentrated at the south gate of the New World Department Store, the east gate of the Shanghai Tower, and the Dongchang Road entrance of the Bund Riverside Avenue. It is prohibited to stop and pick up passengers randomly on main roads.

Shanghai Huangpu River Cruise: Route, Price, Tips
When traveling in Shanghai, you should not miss a cruise tour on the Huangpu River. It is the best way to admire Shanghai's classic skyline views of colonial architecture and modern skyscrapers along the river.
The Huangpu River — "the Mother River of Shanghai"
The Huangpu River, the largest river passing through the city of Shanghai, is honored as the mother river of Shanghai.
It stretches for 113 kilometers (70 miles) with an average width of 400 meters and a depth of 9 meters. It snakes its way through Shanghai and divides the city into two sections: Pudong in the east and Puxi in the west.
It is also the source of most of Shanghai's drinking water, after it goes through a purification process, of course. Today, the Huangpu River is the site of a bustling tourist business in the form of river cruises.
Cruise Route and Price
There are many cruise options which vary in size, capacity, decoration, and amenities. Some boats look very trendy with a modern-style bar, while some are decorated in a traditional Chinese style. The cruises can hold passengers ranging from 80 to 1,000. You can choose a boat based on your interests.
Huangpu River Cruise
There are several tour lengths you can choose from, from a 30-minute cruise to a 3½-hour cruise. The cruises along the Huangpu River often start from the wharf near the Bund, and head towards Yangpu Bridge or Wusongkou International Cruise Terminal, and back again along the opposite side of the river to the Bund.
At present, the most popular one is the 50-minute classic cruise. The cruises are available during the day and night. It is recommended to take a cruise at night when the river is veiled in the sparkling neon lights on both sides.
Cruise route: Shiliupu Wharf near the Bund – Shanghai Tower – Shanghai World Financial Center – Jinmao Tower – Oriental Pearl TV Tower – Yangpu Bridge – Waibaidu Bridge – Monument to the People's Heroes – Peace Hotel – Customs House – back to the wharf
Boarding place: Shiliupu Wharf near the Bund (531 Zhongshan East 2nd Rd)
Duration: about 50 minutes
Cruise operating hours: 11am–9:30pm
Interval: 15–30 minutes
Price: around 150 yuan (≈US$22) (for sightseeing only, without dinner or snacks)
Ticket booking:
1) Tickets can be purchased at Shiliupu Wharf ticket office at Wai Ma Lu 80.
 2) You can buy your ticket online or through ticket agents. Contact us for details. 
 3) Many hotels also provide a ticket booking service; you can check with your hotel.
What to See on the Cruise
A night view of the Bund
On the cruise, you will see the distinctive contrasts between the classical European buildings and soaring modern skyscrapers from the two sides of the Huangpu River.
Besides offering a privileged view of the bridges that span the Huangpu River, the cruise boats also offer an excellent view of the famous colonial-era buildings that make up the Bund on the eastern bank as well as buildings such as the Peace Hotel, with its unique pyramid roof in blazing green, and the Customs House, with its large clock tower.
On the western bank, you will see a bustling metropolis full of modern skyscrapers and towering buildings, such as Jinmao Tower, the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, and Shanghai World Financial Center.
The Best Times to Take a Cruise
The best times to take a cruise on the Huangpu River are March–May and September–November when the weather is pleasant. You can enjoy the scenery on the deck of the boat and have a great opportunity to take clear and awesome pictures.
If you decide to go on a cruise on a cold day, remember to take a coat. It can be very chilly when you stand on the deck. Rainy days will be a little foggy so some of the scenery on the Bund may be obscured.
Nearby Attractions
Yuyuan: It is a classic Chinese garden with rich history and culture. You will see traditional Chinese garden architecture, and exquisite sculptures and carvings.
The Bund: The architecture along the Bund is a living museum of the colonial history of the 1800s.
Nanjing Road is Shanghai's busiest shopping street lined with top-end shopping malls, old-brand shops, and traditional eateries.
Enrich Your Experience with a Huangpu River Cruise
Take a relaxing cruise on the Huangpu River.
It is a great choice to take a relaxing cruise on the Huangpu River after a full day of sightseeing. Stand on the deck to get a feel for the city, and take pictures of the incredible skyline.
